svg.title: Threat model of the macOS Trusted Computing Base
svg.desc: A hand-drawn systems sketch showing attackers on the left, the macOS trusted computing base in the middle, protected assets on the right, and the supply chain above.

g.text: A least-privileged application must not gain authority over the trusted computing base.
Apple build and signing systems • Developer CI and signing keys • Notarization • MDM • Update servers
Threats: compromised build, stolen signing key, malicious update, rollback, malicious management command
Property-relative trust closure: components whose failure can violate the selected security goal
SIP, KIP, PAC and memory rules
XPC, Mach services and privileged helpers
System Extensions, Network Extension and Endpoint Security
User consent, automation and application delegation
Boot integrity • Kernel integrity • User data • Secrets • Privacy • Availability
Dashed red arrows show high-impact paths that require separate threat analysis: physical boot changes, privileged persistence, and supply-chain compromise.
Solid gold arrows show normal authority and data flows that must remain constrained by authentication, authorization, validation, and isolation.
A least-privileged application may request work, but it cannot choose the authority, target, or policy used to perform that work.
